A shopkeeper gives a discount of 25% on the purchase of 20 kg of rice. The cost price of the rice is Rs. 55/kg and the marked price is Rs. 70/kg. The weighing machine of the shopkeeper is faulty, and it shows weight of 1 kg when the actual weight is 800 grams. find the percentage profit of the shopkeeper(rounded off to two decimal places).
e:
Cost price of rice = Rs. 55/kg
Marked price = Rs. 70/kg
Discount given = 25%
The faulty weighing machine shows 1 kg when the actual weight is 900 grams.
SP = MP * (1 - discount percentage) = 70 * (1 - 0.25)
=> Rs. 52.5/kg
Effective selling price for 800 grams of rice is Rs. 52.5 which means the effective selling price per kg (1000 grams) will be :
Effective selling price = 52.5/0.80 = Rs. 65.625/kg
The profit per kg of rice is the difference between the effective selling price and the cost price.
Profit/kg = 65.625 - 55 = Rs. 10.625/kg
Required profit percentage = 10.625/55 * 100 = 19.32%

t: A dishonest dealer sells his goods at 10% loss on the cost price but uses a faulty weight that weighs 30% less. His profit or loss percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) is:

=> 9C/7 or 1.2857C

t: A dishonest seller sells rice at a profit of 23% on cost price and wheat at a profit of 20% on cost price. He also uses a measure of 750 gm instead of 1 Kg. Find the percent profit earned by him, if he sells 1 Kg rice and 1 Kg wheat to a customer.
e:
Let, cost price of 1 Kg rice = Rs.100
And cost price of 1 Kg wheat = Rs.100
Total cost price of 1 Kg rice and 1 Kg wheat = Rs.200
Selling price of 750 gm rice = 100 x 123/100 = Rs.123
Selling price of 1 Kg = 1000 gm rice = 123/750 x 1000 = Rs.164
Selling price of 750 gm wheat = 100 x 120/100 = Rs.120
Selling price of 1 Kg = 1000 gm wheat = 120/750 x 1000 = Rs.160
Total selling price of 1 Kg rice and 1 Kg wheat = 164 + 160 = Rs.324
% profit = (324 - 200)/200 x 100
= 124/200 x 100
= 62%
